U0215.title: Lost Communication With Door Switch A
U0215.description: U0215 means the networked door switch unit A no longer answers. In many doors the switch packs for windows, mirrors and locks are small bus nodes, usually LIN slaves under a door or body module, and the master stores this code once switch A stops replying. The manufacturer decides which door panel carries letter A. U0215 to U0221 cover switches A to G. The buttons on that panel stop working, while the other doors normally keep working.

causes.label: Broken wire in the door hinge area
Water or corrosion in the switch connector
Fault in the door or body module polling the switch

symptoms: Window, lock or mirror buttons on one panel not working
Usually no MIL

U0219.title: Lost Communication With Door Switch E
U0219.description: U0219 means the networked door switch unit E is no longer heard. In modern doors the switch packs for windows, mirrors and locks are often small bus nodes, typically LIN slaves under a door or body module, so each panel can report its own communication loss. The master that polls switch E stores U0219 once its replies stop; GM documents this setting rule for the whole U0100-U02FF range. No manufacturer documents U0219 publicly; GM's U-code list uses its own entries (U0203/U0204) for rear door switch panel modules instead. The letter E is assigned by the maker, so the door concerned must be taken from the vehicle's documentation. U0215 to U0218 and U0220 cover the other switches. Window or lock buttons fail; no MIL.

causes.label: Broken wire in the door hinge area (flexing harness)
Water ingress into the door switch pack
Switch unit E without power or ground

symptoms: Window, mirror or lock buttons in one door inoperative
Switch illumination off
Fault changes when the door is opened or closed
